<!-- Public issues must contain no private repository identities or internal
findings. Use the owning repository's approved internal channels for private
context. Never include protected evaluations, customer/raw data, or credentials.
Use private security reporting for vulnerabilities or accidental disclosures. -->

## Problem and intended outcome

Who is affected, and what should change?

## Proposed scope

Name the interfaces or pages involved. Describe alternatives and
compatibility or migration needs. Discuss private ownership in approved
internal records only.

## Evidence and limits

Link sources approved for the target repository's visibility. For research
claims, identify the endpoint, provenance, uncertainty, and limitations. Public
claims need public evidence. Label planned work and synthetic material.

## Validation and resources

Describe how the change could be checked. State any model/provider execution,
publication, deployment, or budget requirements; the proposal grants no such
authorization.
